svg.text: See the drone, then hit it
One camera system · no radar, no datalink, no GPS on the target · the target is 4–15 pixels across
the whole method, end to end
SEE — three stabilised moments as colour: AP 0.159 → 0.895 on one near-static clip
the static world cancels to grey;
only what moved keeps its colour
this is also how the human labeller found it: flip frames, watch what moves
accuracy and speed in one pass
Same network and settings, on 10_06: single-frame input scores AP 0.159 and the temporal stack 0.895 — though only the temporal arm trains on pasted instances.
the same finding on a different mount: at 3 px, only motion sees it
SEEK — the same idea on an interceptor: four cameras, 360°, one drone among ~50 contacts
it holds station, so the four
a target in a seam is seen
both are right — it is still
contacts a frame and no confidence
Physics does: a fixed object has a
85% of clutter survives the best one-frame gate
and only it may set the range
Motion proposes, appearance disposes. Every metre of detection range buys 0.6 m of defended radius — nothing else in the system trades that steeply.
HIT — a bearing alone is enough to collide with something
simulated flight (Isaac Sim, 20 Hz closed loop)
ACQUIRE holds still on purpose — moving destroys the evidence
a line of sight that does not rotate while
the range shrinks is a collision course
bearing steers (a pixel is a ray); range only schedules speed
sensor latency is declared, not inherited
detector “oracle”: the simulator's own box, zero latency
it measures the guidance law, not the seeker
on the seeker's own detections: 0 / 3, all struck
HOW EVERY NUMBER HERE WAS MEASURED
IoU is meaningless on a 6 px box — a pixel of shift swings it wildly
10_06 is a development video; ARD-MAV / NPS use their own IoU 0.5
two Iris airframes touching are ~0.5 m centre to centre
arriving after the building is hit is a separate, scored failure
two loops and a test suite
Isaac Sim at 20 Hz, and an arithmetic sandbox: 120 scenarios in 1.2 s
a unit-test suite over geometry, guidance, dynamics, the ring and scoring
Detection is measured on real, hand-labelled video. Interception is measured in a closed-loop Isaac Sim renderer — there is no flight test here, and this figure says so on purpose.
